caption:
With Black History Month beginning and International Holocaust Remembrance Day having just passed, this felt like the right moment to reflect and share some of my testimony.

This summer, traveling to Washington DC and Berlin with the USC Shoah Foundation pushed me to learn more about antisemitism, racism, and the deep connections between Black and Jewish histories. Being in these spaces, hearing these stories, and having real conversations reshaped how I understand remembrance, responsibility, and empathy.

I’m incredibly grateful for every meaningful moment and connection along the way. Thank you to the @uscshoahfoundation and @usc_athletics for trusting me with this experience and giving me the opportunity of a lifetime. These lessons stay with me.

caption:
San Giljan ASC is pleased to welcome Alika Naone and Bernardo Herzer to the squad ahead of this season’s European Challenger Cup campaign 🇪🇺

Both players recently concluded their collegiate careers in the United States, competing at the highest level of NCAA water polo, earing All-American honours and named to the Peter J. Cutino Award Watch List. 

Herzer has represented the USA Water Polo Men’s National Team, including participation at the 2025 World Aquatics World Championships, and previously featured with the USA Youth National Team at major global events.

Naone was recognised as the West Coast Conference Newcomer of the Year this season. He also has a strong background in youth national team competition with USA Water Polo, including appearances at the 2018 FINA Men’s World Youth Championships.

They will also be joined by Marko Vavic, who returns to further strengthen the squad, adding additional depth and international experience to our Challenger Cup campaign.

We look forward to integrating all three players as we represent San Giljan ASC on the European stage.

Welcome to San Giljan ⚫️🟡🔴

caption:
Psalm 56:3-4
Been here before, have to go through it again... Hurts to have to undergo another surgery due to a labral tear in the right hip. Facing this setback after all the hard work I put in this fall has been incredibly difficult. I had an amazing first fall here at USC, and I’m so grateful to my coaches and  team for everything they’ve poured into me.

While I won’t be able to compete with the team this season, my support will never fade. I’ll be there every step of the way, having my teammates’ backs and doing whatever I can to help us succeed. Processing what’s happened and the road to recovery hasn't been easy, but I know I’m surrounded by the best people. Thanks to my teammates, coaches, and trainers for the constant support over the last few months. I’ll be heading into this rehab stage with everything I need to come back stronger.

caption:
“The greatest mental strategy I’ve developed since being in college is letting go. 

My freshman year I struggled with dwelling. Being a golfer, it’s easy to dwell when you’re having a tough day, but the more I dwelled and carried the bad shots and holes with me the more they compiled. 

I was setting myself up for failure rather than success. The same for the good things, too — if I kept dwelling on the good things I got too ‘up’ and hurt myself by getting too greedy and aggressive. 

After a shot or hole, good or bad, I acknowledge what happened and look at it from an analytical perspective. I take what I learned and move on with a clear slate with all of my focus and attention on the next shot.”

USC women’s golfer @baileytheshoemaker shares her #1 mental strategy 🧠 💪 

Golf is SO mental. It’s so important to use the time in between shots and holes to your advantage. 

I love Bailey’s thoughts about the importance of letting go, staying in the present moment, and resetting in between every shot 👏 

Fight On Bailey ✌🏻 
And good luck this spring ⛳️ 

#innergameofgolf #collegegolf

caption:
2025 was the dream year. 

Not the perfect year, but the year that I sat in the drivers’ seat in my own life for the first time and lived in the prayers of my younger self. 

I filmed my first Nike campaign (childhood DREAM), graduated from my dream college, went on my first brand trip (x4!!!), hit 100k on instagram + TikTok (hehe), went on my first girls trip (x2!!), NCAA D1 podium finish (my highest championship finish!), chose myself over the sport I gave 14 years to, spent so much time with loved ones, spend so much time alone, started building my first business, started my masters degree, MOVED TO SHANGHAI…. I’ve stepped so far outside of my comfort zone this year and God has been so good to me through it all. 

Praying for another year of health, growth, happiness, authenticity, joy, love, success and everlasting faith for me and for you !!💌♥️

Servite alum Max Thomas returns home — now coaching sprints at Servite High School, working alongside his father Brandon Thomas.

A 4x CIF Div 3 CHAMPION doubling in both the 100 M & 200 M, in 2021, and 2022. 

Legacy in motion.
The standard just went up.

This chapter of my life has closed, but it is just the beginning of a new one. I’m excited to see what God has planned for the future.

caption:
August 2,1991 - December 11, 2025 🤍🕊️

I lost my dear big sister last Thursday. Words cannot describe how much I love and miss her. Telisha was the easiest person to love. She had the most contagious laugh and a way about her that made ordinary moments feel special. You’ve never seen pure love and joy on a little kids face until you’ve seen Telisha come home and my face light up. When I was little the only birthday present my parents would get me is bringing my big sister back home to surprise me (at least that’s the only gift I remember) She was such a bright light in my life.

Losing my older sister so soon still feels unreal, but how blessed am I to feel so much love for one person. You’re in Gods hands now. Be at peace with Him. You watched over me and protected me on this Earth, I know you’ll do it in heaven now. I’ll see you again one day, I love you forever🤍✝️

caption:
It’s March 2025, and JuJu Watkins (@jujubballin) is on fire. The USC Trojans star guard—then a sophomore and largely considered the best player in women's college basketball—has led her team to its deepest NCAA tournament run in decades. Watkins is fearless in the high-stakes, round two game, driving down the court with her power on full display. Suddenly, her right knee buckles and she hits the hardwood. Amid the shock and pain, she’s in denial of what the injury turns out to be: an ACL tear that will sideline her for the rest of the tournament and the entire 2025-2026 season. But even when reality did sink in, the sadness was short-lived. Tap the link in bio to read the full @selfmagazine profile on Watkins, her rehab journey, and the resilience that keeps her charging forward.

caption:
❗️DR❗️ Søgaard-Andersen gør det igen 👊🏼

Landsholdssvømmeren fra Hovedstadens Svømmeklub svømmer 1.42.34 i EM-semifinalen i 200m frisvømning og forbedrer sin danske rekord fra i formiddags med imponerende 1.1 sekund.

Splittider: 23.71-25.81-26.08-26.65

Om rekordløbet siger Oliver Søgaard-Andersen:

”Jeg stolede mere på mig selv her til aften, og jeg lagde ud, som jeg burde gøre. Det koster lidt de sidste meter, men der skal bare mere træning til. Jeg er så tilfreds med den her tid, for det er på dette niveau, jeg har forventet at præstere, så jeg er rigtig glad for så også at gøre det,” siger Oliver Søgaard-Andersen.

HSK-svømmeren slutter på en samlet 12. plads til europamesterskaberne på kortbane og har i løbet af dagen forbedret den tidligere danske rekord med 1,35 sekund.

Endnu en gang kæmpestort tillykke 🇩🇰

caption:
Lauren 🩵

My best friend. My day one. The girl I grew up with on and off the field. From club soccer tournaments, carpool mornings, and our iconic pancake circles before practice that had everyone dying. No matter where life took us, we still showed up for each other’s college games, and that meant everything. The moments I’ll miss the most are the little ones: watching sunsets, getting sweet treats, birthday dinners, and laughing at absolutely nothing until we cried. You had the brightest smile, the loudest laugh, and this way of getting excited over the tiniest things that made every moment feel lighter.

I know God has you now. I know you’re at peace. And I know your spirit is still here in the sunsets, the joy, the little sparks of life you loved so much. Thank you for growing up with me, for loving me like a sister, and for being the kind of friend you never get twice in a lifetime.

I love you forever, LT

caption:
🏌️‍♂️ PEAK GOLF ATHLETE: KAI KOMULAINEN 🟢

Kai started golf at 8 years old and quickly rose through the ranks, winning state junior titles and competing in 4 PGA Tour of Australasia events by age 16. He’s also represented Queensland multiple times and joined the High Performance Program in 2023.

Knowing he wanted to play college golf in the US, Kai began at the University of Tennessee before transferring to the University of Southern California, where he now trains within a world class program and facilities.

Each time Kai returns home to the Gold Coast, we meet in person to review his screen, update his program, and ensure his physical development stays on track. From overseas, we triage any injuries, aches, or pains through video calls to maintain seamless continuity of care.

Kai is fully committed to taking his game to the next level and preparing for a future in professional golf. 💪

Welcome to the #RiseFamily, Rian 🚀

caption:
september is important for so many reasons. the reason it’s so important to me is because it is suicide prevention month. mental health has always been something i’m proud to advocate for and something that has affected me first hand. knowing how i struggled silently for so long has always made me want to share my story so others know they aren’t alone. 

i wanted to show that life can be better on the other side, even when you feel that there’s no hope. it’s not always sunshine but after a storm there can be rainbows. 

i’m not sure who needs to hear this, but no matter what you’re going through there are so many people who love you. even when you feel the most alone, i promise you they’re there. it can take a while to find them, or feel like they’re nowhere near you, but they’re always closer than you think. the amount of people that would feel your absence is astonishing. 

turn to your people, and make sure they know they’re loved. make sure they are okay. the bonds with people are some of the most powerful things man has. 

in a world full of darkness and despair, choose kindness. choose to smile at people. choose to help others, and to love them fully. you will change peoples lives. 💜🩵

#suicidepreventionmonth #youreloved #choosekindness

caption:
7’4 USC Big Gabe Dynes is one of the most unique players heading into the B10 next season. 

Dynes had a strong Sophomore season for Youngstown State where he averaged 7 PPG, 6 RPG and 3 BPG in only 21 Minutes a game while also being named to the all Horizon defensive team. 

At 7’4 Dynes is one of the tallest players in ncaa history and he takes full advantage of his height on both ends. Dynes is a great lob threat offensively who also has strong touch around the rim and on the defensive end he has the ability to protect the rim at the rim and from three. 

Dynes was one of 5 underclassmen since 2008 to have a BLK% of 14 or higher and a TS% of 65 or higher and was the only player in college basketball to hit that mark this past season.

Truly blessed to have signed a professional contract with @on

This is attributed to not only my hard work but to the support I’ve had from my teammates and coaches from AYSO, to Slammers, to Servite, and USC. Throughout this journey I’ve made unbreakable bonds, extended my family, and carried the lessons I’ve learned to help me navigate each step. I would like to give a special thanks to Coach Alex and the Gimenez family for always welcoming and supporting me, to Coach Hayes and Coach Watts for bringing me to USC and giving me the platform to work toward my goals every day, to Coach Jet for instilling a confidence in me that has yet to be broken, and to Coach JB for trusting in me and staying persistent even when it feels like everything is falling apart. None of this would be possible without the sacrifices my parents make for me every single day, I love you guys with my whole heart. Lastly I would like to thank On for this opportunity, going pro in my 4th season of track and field was something I never understood was possible, believe me when I say this is only the beginning…

USC Athletes! 🏋🏽‍♂️

Participate in research and receive a free Therabody device 🎁

We’re running a study at the John McKay Center (JMC) exploring how hand cooling impacts strength and fatigue during upper-body resistance training.

We’re looking for participants:
✅ Ages 18–35
✅ 2–3 years of upper-body training
✅ Not currently in-season or managing upper-body injuries
✅ Female participants must be on a low-dose monophasic oral contraceptive

Only 3 quick sessions (~20 min each) this summer or fall.

💡 Get hands-on with performance tech
🎓 Be part of a cutting-edge study
📲 DM me or scan the flyer to learn more

Not sure if you qualify? Reach out anyway!

Male participants are encouraged to reach out as well; we’re aiming for a balanced study group.

caption:
update: thoughts on my freshman season

  freshman year did not play out how i expected, but the end goal hasn’t changed!
	since january of 2024 i have been dealing with injury, and that continued through my freshman season. nothing major, but minor setbacks kept showing up, leading me to doubt my readiness every time i stepped on the track. 
	my mind has been the biggest obstacle. besides my physical health, my success pre-injury can be attributed to unconditional self-confidence, never doubting if something i wanted was attainable. since then, passion turned into dread of re-injury. that’s not who i am. i grew tired of constantly stepping on the track and feeling like a shadow of myself. it felt like a chore, and it was exhausting not seeing any results from the work i was putting in. it got to a point where i questioned if i was really cut out for this. eventually, i realized that having THAT doubt in myself scared me more than the possibility of re-injury. 
	unfortunately, there are many coaches that would discount their athletes feelings in this situation, but the coaches at SC did anything but. they listened to me and they HEARD me. so after many conversations, we decided to cut my competition season short to focus on getting healthy, rebuilding my confidence, and recovering from burnout by learning to enjoy the process again. 
	thanks to my family and coaches at SC and in OR, i am feeling more and more like myself (mentally and physically!) every day on and off the track. working with great medical staff, i am feeling healthier than i have since before my injury, and i am finally rebuilding the strength that i’ve lost since then.
 i am not “back” yet, but we are making strides in the right direction. in the the mean time, i will continue to be patient and give myself grace. the process may look a little different, but the dream remains the same. 
  if you are struggling with your mental health, injury, self doubt, or burnout, let me be proof that you are not alone. let me know if you have any questions! <3

athlete.bio: A tenacious playmaker from the sun-soaked fields of Southern California, this midfielder combines agility with a keen tactical mind, inspiring teammates with relentless energy and an infectious passion for the game.

caption:
Ha llegado el momento de despedirme del club que ha sido mi casa desde 2014. Llegué con una mochila más grande que yo y unos sueños aún más grandes—llena de orgullo, ilusión y esperanza. En estos más de 10 años, he crecido en cada etapa: desde la cantera hasta las categorías más altas, de largos viajes en autobús a torneos inolvidables. He vivido la euforia de las victorias, la tristeza de las derrotas y he aprendido de cada reto y de cada momento hermoso entre medias.

Este club no solo me formó como futbolista—me formó como persona. He aprendido valores que llevaré conmigo el resto de mi vida. Me siento orgullosa de haberme formado en este club, en este país, y estaré eternamente agradecida a todas las personas que han sido parte de este camino: mis compañeras, entrenadores, cuerpo técnico, administración y amistades.

A mis compañeras: gracias por las batallas, las risas, los recuerdos y por exigirme siempre lo mejor de mí. Ha sido un honor llevar este escudo junto a vosotras.
A mis entrenadores: gracias por creer en mí y por ayudarme a crecer.

Al Atleti: gracias por todo. Siempre llevaré una parte de ti conmigo.

Eternamente agradecida. Eternamente una de las tuyas.
Siempre Atleti. (2014–2025) ❤️🤍

caption:
#7 signing off ✍️

5 years with this club… it’s hard to even put into words how much it’s meant to me. this has been so much more than just a place to play soccer, it’s been a place where I grew as a player, as a teammate, and as a person. thank you to the coaches and everyone who believed in me, challenged me, and gave me the space to pour my heart into this game I love so much.

to my girls… where do I even start? you’ve been more than teammates, you’ve been my family. you stuck with me through every high and low, and I’ll never forget how you embraced me, even with my strong passion for this sport. I know my intensity could be a lot at times, but you never made me feel like too much. Instead, you supported me, matched my energy, and made this journey so special.

we’ve shared unforgettable memories: the big wins, the tough losses, the late-night team talks, the endless laughter, and all the little moments in between that made these years so meaningful. the friendships I’ve made here have left a permanent impact on my heart, and I’ll carry them with me forever.

I’m so thankful, so grateful, and so blessed to have had the privilege of playing alongside the most incredible group of girls. this isn’t goodbye, because the bond we’ve built goes way beyond the field. 🤍

onto phase 2 👀

caption:
Я сломалась. Устала. 
Так я думала три месяца назад после завершения студенческого сезона. Профессиональный спорт - это тяжело.  Ты жертвуешь многим, а вернее всем — ради доли секунды и победы. Думаю, каждый в карьере проходил через выгорание — момент, когда хочется всё бросить и не возвращаться к этой исходной точке.
За три месяца я поняла: проблемы будут всегда. Усталость - тоже. И выгорание тоже будет, но если ты любишь что то всем сердцем…🤍

И вот я снова здесь. Снова стою в 7 утра с сеткой в руках, надеваю очки и шапочку. 
Я скучала и очень счастлива вернуться. 
Каждому человеку нужен отдых. Перезагрузка. Вот и мне она была необходима. 
Без каких-либо ожиданий от себя пошла наматывать свои километры :) 

College season ended, and I hit a wall.
I was tired — mentally, physically, emotionally.
One of those moments when you just wanna quit and never come back 💔 but here I’m! 3 months later I’m back in the water with a full heart and a whole new appreciation for how much I missed it❤️‍🩹

caption:
“What does football mean to me? It’s almost everything. I don’t want to say it’s everything, because it’s not everything, but it’s close to everything. It’s what I’ve been doing my entire life. It’s what I watched on TV growing up, and I imagined myself being there one day. 

I could say that football is joy and happiness but that would barely be explaining it. It’s a feeling that’s almost inexplicable. I wouldn’t even be able to imagine a life without football.” 🏈

Junior defensive lineman @braylanshelby is working day in and day out to take his game to the next level and achieve his goals. But it doesn’t happen without the passion for playing the game, the dedication to perfecting his craft that he so clearly demonstrates✌️

Words cannot describe how grateful I am for these past 16 years of my life. Swimming has been a part of my every day since I can remember, and now it’s finally time to move on to new adventures in life. This sport has given me friendships that I will carry with me the rest of my life. I have been given opportunities that I never could have dreamed off all because of this sport. I have learned so many life lessons and have grown in so many different ways🥹

Thank you to USC Swim for being my home for the past 4 years. Getting to serve as Captain in my final season was such an honor. Thank you to all my coaches for believing in me and for pouring yourselves into my swimming career these past few years! This experience was truly life changing✌️ @uscswim 

Thank you to all of my past club coaches, from helping me find my place in the pool as a little girl, to helping me get through high school while working to achieve all my goals🫶🏼 @guelphrocks @kylepinsonneault8 

Thank you to all my past and present teammates for always encouraging me, cheering me on, and helping me be my best self! This sport wouldn’t be half as amazing without all the memories I’ve made over the years with the people I’ve shared the pool with💖

Thank you to my family for all the sacrifices over the years to help get me to this point. I will never be able to express how much your support means to me❤️

Swimming will always have a place in my heart, and for now all I can say is thank you and fight on forever✌️

caption: after transferring to usc in the spring last year and spending my first season as a trojan trying to get back in shape while also trying to jump far, i was so excited to be here in the fall and get the base training i didn’t get last season. i would call my mom everyday telling her how great i felt and how much stronger and bouncier i was. i knew this season was the season for me to jump far and prove myself on this team….and then i got injured🙂. being a triple jumper, an ankle injury was the last thing i needed. and me being me, i kept jumping on it because i wanted so badly to jump far especially after how rough last season went. so i jumped through the pain and limped out the pit each meet just trying to get a further mark. i went to rehab twice a week and tried about three different pain meds. i’ve never had an injury before, not even shin splints so dealing with this wasn’t just challenging physically but mentally too. and after finally figuring out how to take my pain meds so they work the best, conference is already here and i don’t have a far enough mark to go. which means my season is over. i actually can’t even explain how upsetting it is lol. especially because i know i’m better than what i’ve shown. i know what i can do, i know how far i can jump, but i guess it wasn’t my time yet. so for now all i can do is get healthy and be grateful that i have another year of eligibility. God has a plan for me and all i can do is trust him. i will be back healthier and stronger next year❤️

athlete.name: Mackenzie Miller
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor from the beaches of SoCal, this athlete fuses agility with finesse, showcasing an unyielding spirit. Known for her infectious energy, she inspires teammates both on and off the field.

caption:
After a lot of thought and reflection, I’ve made the difficult decision to step away from volleyball. It’s not a choice that came easily but over time, I realized that my passion for the sport had slowly faded, especially this past year. What once brought me joy, drive, and excitement started to feel more like a burden than a blessing. I tried to push through, hoping that spark would come back and things would get better, but it never truly did. I had to be honest with myself, and continuing for the sake of obligation wasn’t doing me any good mentally or emotionally.
Walking away from something that’s been such a big part of my life for the past 11 years is by far the hardest thing I’ve ever done. Through this sport, I’ve met some of my best friends and women I know will stand beside me for the rest of my life, future bridesmaids and lifelong sisters. While I may be closing this chapter, I’m incredibly grateful for everything volleyball has given me, and I wouldn’t trade the moments had for anything in the world. 
With this decision, I’m also stepping away from USC. I’m so thankful for all the amazing people I’ve met, the hard lessons I’ve learned, and the memories I’ve made during my time here. While not every experience was what I expected—or what I deserved—it’s all shaped me into the person I am today. USC will always hold a special place in my heart, even if some aspects of the journey were harder than they had to be.
Thank you to everyone who always supported me and all my club coaches throughout the years for believing in me. But mostly, thank you to my parents, who made every part of my journey possible giving me every opportunity in the world.❤️❤️❤️

athlete.name: Dillon Klein
athlete.bio: A strategic playmaker with a background in competitive gymnastics, this versatile athlete blends agility and finesse on the court. Known for relentless determination and a charismatic team spirit, they inspire teammates daily.

caption:
FIRST TEAM ALL-AMERICAN: Dillon Klein

Klein represents the 35th first-team certificate earned by a Trojan and is the first since setter Micah Christenson was chosen for first-team
laurels in 2015. It is the first time since 2012 that USC has had more than one All-America award winner (Tony Ciarelli, first team/Player of the Year; Henry Cassiday, second team; Christenson, second team). Klein and Tomkinson are the fourth and fifth All-Americans to be honored under head coach Jeff Nygaard.

Klein ranked second in the MPSF for kills (3.84 kps, 13th nationally) and points (4.48 kps, 15th nationally), and was third in attacks (7.98 aps) and hitting percentage (.355). He reached double-digit kills 20 times (61 in his career), double-digit points 21 times, and produced a pair of double-doubles. Klein was chosen for the AVCA’s National Player of the Week award twice and earned Molten/MPSF Player of the Week awards three times (two offensive, one defensive). He also reached the 1,000-kill mark in his career this season ✌️

Happy Birthday Mom!

🎉🥳🥳🎉

To my biggest supporter! To the woman who has been my inspiration my whole life. To the late night calls and infinite wisdom on stain removal, flower arrangements, and interior design.

You probably wouldn’t have known it when you gave it to me the day I left for college, but this note would travel with me almost everywhere I’d go and to every track meet for at least the next 4 years.

College hasn’t been an easy ride for me, and that note is something I can always look to when I need inspiration. It’s a constant reminder of who this is all for.

I’m beyond thankful to have you as my mom, and I hope you have the best day 🎉

Love ya!

La historia de Toño Safa, un golfista mexicano que, con solo 14 años, dejó su casa, su familia y su país para perseguir el sueño de convertirse en profesional. it’s almost been a week since this moment, but I still don’t have the words to explain this euphoric feeling🤯

az összes interjúban elmondtam már 100x, de bármikor elmondom még 100x, hogy mennyire büszke vagyok a lányokra❤️ ezt igazán oda tettük és sikerült, első magyar váltóérem a SC világbajnokságon!! WE ARE MAKING HISTORY‼️ és ez még csak az eleje ennek a csodás váltónak. köszönöm hogy a része lehettem ennek a váltónak, és hogy biztatok bennem és ezerrel szurkoltatok az egész 200 méteren keresztül, amit még a vízben is hallottam❤️

thank you to all of my coaches, teammates, family, friends, and everyone who watched and cheered us on♥️ 

hálás vagyok az Újpesti csapattársaimnak, hogy kijöttetek szurkolni nekünk, és különösen hálás vagyok Zoli Bának, hogy hitt bennem az egész verseny alatt mikor bizonytalan voltam.

last but not least, köszönöm az összes szurkolónak, és önkéntesnek, akik egy része lehettek ennek a sikernek. Olyan hangulat robbant ki az arénában a döntő alatt, amivel azt az utolsó erőt adtátok, hogy célba érjünk ezüstéremre 🤗

(ahogy az utolsó képen láthatjátok…) puszi mindenkinek és kellemes ünnepeket🎄☺️❤️

athlete.name: Micah Williams
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with lightning-fast footwork, this sprinter thrives on challenges. Hailing from a vibrant community, they blend passion and precision, inspiring teammates with an unwavering commitment to excellence.

caption:
The past two years have been the hardest of my life. From being one of the best in the world—making Olympic and Championship teams—to hitting rock bottom, I’ve faced challenges I never thought I would.

This year alone, I’ve had 4 surgeries: 2 on my knees and 2 on my eyes. Hearing a doctor say the words “career-ending” broke me. I felt lost, discouraged, and even thought about quitting.

Some might assume, “Micah, you played football—that’s why your knees are bad.” But the truth is, my knee problems started my first year at Oregon. I ran through pain, took meds just to compete, and kept it all to myself.

But through these struggles, I’ve grown in ways I never imagined. I learned that I’m so much more than just a track athlete. While recovering, I explored new passions—I built wrecked cars, picked up photography, and found purpose beyond the sport.

I’m incredibly grateful to USC for believing in me. They’ve treated my injuries with care, connected me with top doctors, and given me a second chance.

To anyone facing tough times: I hope my story shows you that setbacks don’t define you—they shape you. I’ll be back soon, stronger than ever.

Stay tuned. The best is yet to come. ✌🏽

I am deeply grateful to be part of the Dexcom U team and the community it supports.

I am officially an Olympic finalist!!!

Am I disappointed that I didn’t fully demonstrate what I’m capable of? Not at all. Of course, I would have loved to showcase a better performance in the final, but on the other hand, I never could have imagined the progress I’ve made over the past few years, both professionally and personally. It gives me more motivation to attack and continue to work even more on my potential 💪🏻.

I would like to thank my coach @pb._coaching who has struggled with me over the last 3 years and has always pulled me up. I would like to say thank you to my whole family who supports me at all times. I would like to thank @katelyn_fung_ for flying halfway around the world to watch and support me at the biggest competition in the world. caption:
Join us in congratulating NYS alum Preston Beery for winning Gatorade Nevada Boys Track & Field Player of the Year! He shattered the Nevada high school record for shot put (68’-10”) at Faith Lutheran, and will be continuing his athletic career at USC this fall!

With his award, Preston was given $1,000 to donate to any 501c3 nonprofit organization of his choice that supports young athletes. He has decided to generously donate this money back to NYS to help kids like him, as he played basketball and flag football with us back in the day.

Beery stated, “As a young kid, I was very uncoordinated and even though there is still the competitive aspect, NYS gave me the opportunity to progress in my coordination. It also showed me what sports I enjoy, granted, I like all sports, but NYS set a foundation for them to learn and to grow.”

Congratulations Preston and thank you for giving back to support the next generation of athletes! We can’t wait to see the amazing things to do at USC! #nysnevada #youthsports #community #nysalum #GatoradePOY

Please welcome graduate transfer middle blocker Guy Genis to the Trojan family!

Genis won back-to-back NCAA championships with UCLA (2023, ’24) during three seasons with the Bruins. He is a three-time MPSF All-Academic Team member and a two-time selection to UCLA’s Athletic Director’s Honor Roll (2021, ’22). He appeared in 76 matches and saw action in 245 sets for the Bruins. Genis compiled 316 kills (1.29 kps) with a .463 career hitting percentage and recorded 260 blocks (1.06 bps). He also had 75 digs, 21 service aces, and 19 assists while averaging 1.97 points per set.

But In those darkest moments you brought me friends, teammates, and family that would bring me back. You gave me memories and people that I will treasure forever. You’ve seen me grow stronger, smarter, and eventually you turned me into the man I am today. I can’t thank you enough for the lessons you brought and the family you gave me. I can’t tag everyone who has made an impact on me through my time here but most of you know who you are. Georgetown will always hold a special place in my heart🫶🏽 

Best,

caption:
I’m excited to announce that I will be committing to University of Southern California! ❤️💛

I am very proud that I will be continuing my education and track career at a D1 college and I can’t express how grateful I am for this opportunity.  I want to thank Coach Harris for giving me this opportunity. Thank you to my Teammates for being a Family to me,  I couldn’t have done this without you.  I also want to give a special thanks to my Family and Coach for being there every step of the way.  I want to thank my Coach, mentor and my family, Carlos.  You have taught me so much in so little time.  I cannot ever show how much you mean to me or thank you enough.  And I want to say my final thank you to my Brother, Mom and Dad.  My brother Jake you are the best and favorite training partner but more importantly my best friend.  My Mom being there everyday with me on bad and good days always by the finish line and supporting me on the side I can’t thank her enough and love you Mom.  My Dad I’m so grateful to have you in my life every day I want to get better and I want to make you proud because I see the struggles you do to get me here with the long drives taking me to school and taking me back home being there in the cold for soccer games or waking up early for me to take me to practices thank you for everything love you guys!

With everything said I can’t wait to start my new journey at my new home and face new challenges and I can’t wait to see what’s the future has in store for me! #fighton✌️

With love,

Christine M. Mallard

caption:
Dear former NZ record holder 

Ever since the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria. You broken a national record that nobody was able to touch for 28 years until yesterday. You set an example of how kiwis can fly including me Inspiring all over the nation for decades. I was amazed that following your footsteps and now I am a national record holder just like you were. The way you’ve inspire me to become the greatest in the country one day. I knew it wasn’t going to be a easy road  since everyone in New Zealand wanted to break your national record. They was times I wanted to quit but deep down we all know you and I would’ve been disappointed that it wasn’t me  who broke the record like you wanted me to. Till yesterday, the NZ record is finally broken, all the hard work has paid off and I’m thankful that it was you that was holding it for 28 years.That given me the perseverance and courage to one day break it and keep it in the Nketia family in name. As 28 years ago, you wouldn’t expected your son to break a long standing national record. Well i wasn’t expected to break the record so soon and make the semis at the highest level of competition at this age. Thank you for inspiring me and now I’m a athlete that you always wanted me to be. 

Yours truly
Newest national record holder 
@alishalovrich

caption:
So thankful for this day (1/14/20) with Kobe Bryant, these trainers and the WNBA players. Can’t explain how special I felt being invited to attend this event at Mamba and how comfortable they all made me feel.  I know it is hard to believe that this day changed my life, but it really did.  Been thinking about Kobe and the tragedy a lot lately and it still breaks my heart.  I miss my old life of training, playing in games/tourneys, hanging with teammates, traveling, meeting new ballers from all over the country, teasing Coach, and doing basketball 24/7.  I miss seeing Kobe, Gigi and the entire Mamba team upstairs at Mamba. 
I pray that things will get better again soon and trust God’s plan always.  Mamba mentality forever.  RIP and thank you 🙏🏼🖤🕊🐍 #llkb #llg #mambamentality #godsplan
